headline: SSR MINING PAYS $464M FOR NEVADA'S CONVERSE GOLD — 5.2MOZ RESOURCE SITS 6KM FROM MARIGOLD COMPLEX
snippet: SSR Mining (Nasdaq: SSRM) announced October 12 that it will acquire Roxmore Resources and its Converse gold project in Nevada for C$6.75 per share in cash — an enterprise value of approximately $464 million — plus a new exploration spinout of Roxmore's other assets funded with US$10 million. The Converse project lies 6 kilometres west of SSR's Marigold complex on the Battle Mountain–Eureka Trend and contains 2.2 million ounces indicated (103Mt at 0.65 g/t) and 3.0 million ounces inferred (218Mt at 0.43 g/t); SSR targets 150,000–170,000 oz/yr production over a 10-year mine life with first gold targeted for 2033, backed by $800–900 million in initial capital the company says it will fund entirely from its existing cash position.

headline: GOLD FIGHTS BACK TO $4,187 AHEAD OF SEPTEMBER CPI — DOLLAR AT 18-MONTH HIGH, RATE HIKE ODDS AT 85% BY DECEMBER
snippet: Spot gold traded at $4,186.90 on October 13 — up 0.39% on the session — as Treasury yields and the dollar briefly retreated ahead of the September Consumer Price Index print due October 14 at 8:30 a.m. ET, with Gulf tensions adding a safe-haven bid that offset the greenback's 18-month high. The CME FedWatch tool is pricing an 85% probability of at least one additional Fed rate hike by December, and economists forecast headline September CPI at 3.6–3.7% year-over-year — up from 3.4% in August — meaning a hot print that drives gold below the $4,100 200-day moving average support level could deepen the pullback in TSX-V and ASX exploration stocks already down 18–25% from summer highs.

headline: ENERGY FUELS REWRITES $1.9B MINE-TO-MAGNET DEAL — SUPPLY DISPUTE AT E-VAC MAGNETICS FORCES AMENDMENT
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) disclosed October 13 that it has amended the terms of its $1.9 billion acquisition of Vacuumschmelze (VAC) — Germany's largest permanent magnet maker — to address an ongoing supply contract dispute at e-VAC Magnetics, with adjustments to debt repayment terms and purchase price mechanisms in the event the dispute causes value impairment before closing. The amended deal preserves Energy Fuels' goal of building the first integrated mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain in North America — linking its White Mesa uranium/REE mill in Utah through VAC's 2,000-tonne-per-year magnet plant in Sumter, South Carolina — with regulatory approvals still expected to push the closing into early 2027.

headline: SOUTH AFRICA'S THREE BIG RARE EARTH PROJECTS TARGETING 12,400 TONNES REO/YR BY 2034 — CHINA ALTERNATIVE TAKES SHAPE
snippet: Three key South African rare earth projects could collectively deliver approximately 12,400 tonnes of total rare earth oxide equivalent per year by 2034, according to an October 13 Mining.com.au analysis framing South Africa as the most credible near-term non-China alternative for Western buyers. The report lands just as China's November 10 heavy rare earth export control deadline and January 1, 2027 US DFARS restrictions on Chinese REE in defence contracts create a narrow window in which South African projects with existing feasibility work and infrastructure connectivity could command strategic premium pricing.

headline: QMINES PONTOON HOLE BEATS MODEL AT MT CHALMERS — 16.7M @ 1.04% CU, 1.16G/T AU, 26G/T AG IN QUEENSLAND
snippet: QMines (ASX: QML) reported that the Pontoon hole at its Mt Chalmers volcanogenic massive sulphide copper-gold project in central Queensland returned 16.7 metres at 1.04% copper, 1.16 g/t gold, and 26 g/t silver — a result the company says beat its geological model and confirms grade continuity across the system. Mt Chalmers is an advanced project with a scoping study in place targeting a low-capital restart, and the Pontoon result directly validates the VMS grade assumptions that underpin its economics at a moment when junior copper projects with demonstrated grade continuity are increasingly sought out by investors positioned for the structural copper deficit.

headline: MANY PEAKS MINERALS: 46.75M @ 7.02G/T AU FROM 775M DEPTH AT OUARIGUE — GRADE IMPROVES STEEPLY WITH DEPTH
snippet: Many Peaks Minerals (ASX: MPK) reported that hole FNDC166 at the Ouarigue target of its Ferké Gold Project in Côte d'Ivoire returned 46.75 metres at 7.02 g/t gold from 775.2 metres depth — including a 1.85-metre interval at 109.8 g/t gold — confirming that grade improves significantly with depth at a project that already hosts a 1.3-million-ounce resource at 1.54 g/t. The result sets up a high-priority drill target for the RC program due to resume in October, with investors watching whether the deep high-grade shoots can be traced upward into economics-grade bulk tonnage that could materially upgrade the project's value.

headline: TERRA METALS HITS 194M @ 1.01G/T PGE3 FROM 15M — SOUTHWEST DANTE PGM SYSTEM WIDENS BEYOND RESOURCE BOUNDARY
snippet: Terra Metals (ASX: TM1) reported that RC pre-collar SWRC106 at the Southwest prospect of its Dante PGM project returned 194 metres at 1.01 g/t platinum-palladium-gold equivalent (PGE3) from just 15 metres depth — including a 9-metre interval at 3.53 g/t PGE3 — one of the widest shallow PGM intercepts reported anywhere in 2026. The Southwest prospect sits entirely outside Terra's current Dante resource estimate, and pending diamond drill assays from holes completed to depths between 724 and 918 metres will determine how far the high-grade sulphide mineralisation extends — with positive results pointing to significant resource-growth potential.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $14,636 AS CHILE'S STRIKE SEASON EXTENDS — CENTINELA, CODELCO AND ESCONDIDA ALL DISRUPTED SIMULTANEOUSLY
snippet: LME copper held near $14,636 per tonne on October 13 — less than $250 below September's all-time record high of $14,875 — as Antofagasta's Centinela strike, Codelco's El Teniente suspension from landslide damage, and Escondida government mediation kept Chilean output constrained entering the sixth week of rolling disruptions. Analysts note this combination of record prices and simultaneous multi-mine disruptions is historically unusual and that each week of lost output deepens the structural supply deficit underpinning the AI data-centre and electrification copper supercycle thesis.

headline: POWER MINERALS DRILLS 91M @ 7.7% TREO AT MORRO DO FERRO — BRAZIL RARE EARTH RACE ACCELERATES AS LYNAS MOVE SHIFTS FOCUS
snippet: Power Minerals (ASX: PNN) reported that hole MFSR-055 at its Morro do Ferro rare earth project in Minas Gerais, Brazil returned 91 metres at 7.7% total rare earth oxide content (TREO) from surface — including 1.4% medium-to-heavy rare earth oxide content (MREO) — the highest whole-hole grade result reported from the program and among the highest from any ionic clay project globally in 2026. The result adds urgency to the company's preparation of a maiden resource estimate just as Brazil has become the focal point of Western rare earth investment, with Lynas agreeing this month to acquire Meteoric Resources' 1.63-billion-tonne Caldeira ionic clay project in the same country.

headline: REAL YIELDS, FED NOISE AND CPI WEEK: WHY GOLD ISN'T BEHAVING THE WAY RATE HAWKS EXPECT
snippet: A GoldSilver.com analysis from CPI week examines why gold has held its ground near $4,150–$4,200 despite real yields rising and the US dollar hitting 18-month highs — attributing the resilience to a central bank demand floor that has established a durable structural bid below $4,100. The piece also revisits the August CPI precedent (released September 11) when core inflation ran a tenth of a point hot and gold and silver rallied 1.5–2% anyway, raising the possibility that even a hot September CPI print may not break gold decisively lower — a scenario with direct implications for junior mining investors trying to gauge Q4 sector re-entry risk.
